With scouts surrounding United’s academy games right now, it’s imperative Musa takes every opportunity to put himself in the shop window for a loan that can kickstart his senior career.

Sports.title: Who could YOUR club sign this summer? The stars who will be free agents after Bernardo Silva's Man City exit was confirmed - including three Man United players and European icons
Sports.content:
One of the first players confirmed to be a free agent in the summer is Manchester City captain Bernardo Silva.

City assistant manager Pep Lijnders confirmed the long-serving midfielder will be leaving the Etihad at the end of the season when his contract comes to an end, with his wife, Ines, thought to struggle with English culture.

It comes after nine years of service to Pep Guardiola, but the Spaniard is now faced with the task of replacing one of his star men.

The announcement of Silva's departure is one of the first that can be expected over the coming months. Though the World Cup is a big area of focus for the summer, club football does not rest and the futures of many are still to be decided.

But who is out of contract and up for grabs? Who do we know for sure will be looking for a new team? And who is praying that someone, anyone, will take a chance on them?

Here, Daily Mail Sport puts together a free agent XI of players who are on the hunt for a new deal of some kind.

Manchester City captain Bernardo Silva will leave the club this summer after nine years

It is thought that Silva's wife, Ines, is not a huge fan of English culture despite her husband's lengthy stay at City

GK: Manuel Neuer

Now 40, legendary goalkeeper Manuel Neuer only really deals in one-year contract extensions. Last February, he penned a deal until the end of this season, but we are long past that time this year with no agreement met.

In January, he hinted at another extension, saying: 'I'm feeling positive about the situation. I want to try and produce good performances over the next few months. I think it will be decided towards the end of March or at the beginning of April.'

Tick tock, Manuel.

Manuel Neuer, 40, deals in one-year contracts at Bayern Munich, but is yet to agree terms for next season

RWB: Dani Carvajal

Real Madrid captain Dani Carvajal has been a loyal servant to his club, being contracted to Madrid since he was a child with well over 400 first team appearances to his name.

He's 34 now, though, and Trent Alexander-Arnold is the new shiny toy at right back. He has been limited to just 18 appearances this season - 12 in the league - due to a combination of injuries and selection, and it could be time for him to move on.

Still, he is seen as a stalwart of Madrid's side, and, if he can prove his fitness, an extension to his reported £175,000-a-week deal is not off the cards.

Real Madrid captain Dani Carvajal has found himself down the pecking order at the Bernabeu

CB: Ibrahima Konate

It's been a year of debate around Ibrahima Konate's future. The France centre back, 26, is in his prime and arguably the most valuable player on this list in terms of market price, but Liverpool just cannot get a new deal over the line.

Word is that a number of top European sides are interested in his services, though Real Madrid pulled out of any potential deal earlier this season.

It has been reported that he is earning as little as £70,000-a-week - way down on what some of Europe's top players take home - so may be looking for a hike on that front. Whether Liverpool can offer that is another matter.

He won't be short of suitors if he does leave, but it feels it would be a shame if he did, with Liverpool arguably the best place for him to continue from a footballing point of view.

Ibrahima Konate (left), meanwhile, is yet to agree new terms with Liverpool amid European interest

CB: John Stones

Another who has been at his club for a number of years, John Stones is arguably a Manchester City legend - but will almost certainly leave this summer.

The 31-year-old, thought to be on around £250,000 a week, can't string two games together and has been limited to just 15 appearances this season. A world class centre back at his best, that seems to be in the past now, and it's a doubt whether he will make the England squad for the World Cup in the summer.

He will likely wave goodbye to City after 10 years - but may not be done with football yet.

CB: Harry Maguire

Talks have been ongoing for a while around a new contract for Harry Maguire at Manchester United, but any new deal is yet to be confirmed.

A former United captain and former £80million defender, Maguire is on a reported £190,000-a-week. Though he still very much has a role to play with the Red Devils - and maybe England - that is too much for that very role.

If he does sign a new deal, it's expected he will take a hefty pay cut. But after a rise in form under Michael Carrick and resilience to stay at the club and fight for his place, he has probably earned himself a new deal.

Daily Mail Sport reported two weeks ago that Maguire is close to agreeing a contract that will keep him at Manchester United next season - but wants to know he is still valued by the club.

England defenders Harry Maguire (left) and John Stones (right) will see their deals at Manchester Untied and Manchester City respectively end

LWB: Andy Robertson

Scotland captain Andy Robertson is another Liverpool player on this list, but one feels that his potential departure would hit a little harder for Reds fans than Konate's.

Robertson joined Liverpool for a measly £8.5million in the summer of 2017, and went on to become a main character in the Jurgen Klopp era, winning the Champions League and two Premier League titles at the club.

Now, though, he is behind Milos Kerkez in the pecking order and it remains to be seen whether he will sign a new deal at Anfield. He seemed set to join Tottenham in January, but rejected that approach in favour of staying. The fact the club were willing to let him go, though, may mean the writing is on the wall.

One feels that the Reds could do a lot worse than have Robertson as their back-up left back next season - and probably beyond.

It remains to be seen whether Liverpool will offer Andy Robertson fresh terms for next season

CM: Bernardo Silva

The latest name to be confirmed to be on his way in the summer is Silva. The Portugal international made it clear to reporters at the Club World Cup last June that this would be his final campaign but had stopped short of making an official announcement.

Silva is gunning to secure a seventh Premier League title before his departure, with City nine points behind leaders Arsenal with a game in hand.

The 31-year-old, who believes it is too early for a return to Benfica, has options in the MLS while Juventus have hoped to persuade him into signing.

CM: Casemiro

It was on January 22 that Manchester United confirmed Casemiro would be leaving the club at the end of the season. After a tough three years in red, the Brazil midfielder has found form this year, and United could be reconsidering their decision.

He is, though, earning £350,000-a-week. No chance he would earn that in any new deal.

'I will carry Manchester United with me throughout my entire life,' Casemiro said in a statement. 'From the first day that I walked out at this beautiful stadium, I felt the passion of Old Trafford and the love that I now share with our supporters for this special club.'

Inter Miami are the front-runners to sign him. But don't rule out another year at United just yet.

It was confirmed in January that Casemiro will leave Manchester United after four years

RW: Mohamed Salah

Arguably the biggest name in this team, Mohamed Salah is a bit of an anomaly.

The Liverpool icon will depart Anfield at the end of the season, but he isn't actually out of contract. After a long-running summer saga last year, he penned a two-year deal to stay at the club, but this year hasn't gone to plan.

Whether it's confidence or ability, the Egyptian King looks a shadow of his former self in Liverpool red. Despite that, he has still picked up 19 goal involvements - 10 goals and nine assists - in 35 games.

But the time has come for him to say goodbye and it was announced at the end of last month that the 33-year-old will be looking for a new club in the summer.

Whether that is a top European side or a team elsewhere, Salah is well and truly now on his farewell tour as a Liverpool player.

Mohamed Salah will tear up his two-year Liverpool contract in search of a new challenge

LW: Jadon Sancho

The nightmare that has been Jadon Sancho's Manchester United career will finally come to an end in the summer when his £250,000-a-week deal expires.

Things haven't been the same for the former England winger since a public fall out with former manager Erik ten Hag in 2023. That, plus a pretty sensational dip in form since, may well leave him scrambling around for clubs.

That said, he has had loan spells with Chelsea and Aston Villa in the last two years, but the Blues did pay to ensure they didn't have to make his temporary stay permanent.

The 26-year-old has one goal and three assists in 31 appearances in all competitions this season.

ST: Robert Lewandowski

Robert Lewandowski has done the rounds at some of Europe's top clubs, playing for the likes of Borussia Dortmund, Bayern Munich, and now Barcelona. And, to summarise his career, he scored goals wherever he has played.

But he is now 37, and there is continued uncertainty around his future. His Barca contract is up at the end of the season, and it appears officials at the club are torn on whether to offer him a new one.

He'll have the World Cup off after Poland failed to qualify in the latest international break, and it will be a summer of big decisions on both the club and player's side.

If he does leave, despite his age, he will have no shortage of suitors.

Manchester United's Jadon Sancho (left) and Barcelona's Robert Lewandowski (second right) could be looking for new clubs

Honourable mentions

Marcos Senesi seems set to leave Bournemouth in the summer with there being little breakthrough in contract talks. Barcelona are thought to be one of the clubs interested.

Antonio Rudiger has run his contract down at Real Madrid, but it appears a new one-year deal is on the verge of being agreed.

Andreas Christensen is another former Chelsea defender who could leave Spain, with his contract at Barcelona up soon. He has fallen down the pecking order at the Catalan giants.

Harry Wilson will have no shortage of suitors if he opts to leave Fulham. The Wales winger is having the season of his life in London, registering 11 goals and six assists in all competitions.

Leon Goretzka will leave Bayern Munich in the summer after nine years. The midfielder has been linked with Fenerbahce and AC Milan as potential destinations for next season.

Julian Brandt has been with Borussia Dortmund since 2019 but will depart this summer. The German club have confirmed the midfielder's deal will not be renewed, and he is already on the hunt for a new club.

Sports.title: World Series winner and ex-New York Yankees coach Tom Nieto dies suddenly at age 65
Sports.content:
World Series winner and ex-New York Yankees coach Tom Nieto dies suddenly at age 65

Tom Nieto, a World Series winner in 1987 with the Minnesota Twins, has died suddenly at the age of 65.

The Twins announced the news on social media on Monday afternoon following an announcement from his sister on social media, who said he died of a heart attack.

'On Friday March 27th, my brother Tom passed on after a heart attack, leaving cherished memories in Florida with his family' she wrote. 'His strength and resilience will continue to inspire us all.'

Nieto played in the 1985 World Series with St. Louis Cardinals, losing 4-3 to the Kansas City Royals despite his team taking a 2-0 lead.

Two years later, with the Twins, Nieto was on the winning side when they defeated the Cardinals 4-3.

'The Twins organization mourns the loss of 1987 World Series champion, Tom Nieto. Our thoughts are with the Nieto family in their time of grieving,' the team said in a statement on Monday.

Tom Nieto, a World Series winner in 1987 with the Minnesota Twins, has died suddenly

Nieto worked with New York Yankees and crosstown rivals, the Mets, in his coaching career

As a coach, Nieto was best known for his work in New York. He spent seven years with the Yankees from 1995-2002 and three years with the Mets from 2005.

Under manager Willie Randolph at the Mets, Nieto worked as catching instructor and later as first base coach.

Nieto also played for the Montreal Expos and Philadelphia Phillies across the course of his career.

The Twins traded for him and brought him to Minnesota from the Expos, where he played 41 games for the team in their World Series-winning season.

He also was manager of Rochester Red Wings, the triple-A affiliate of the Washington Nationals.

'Tom was a respected leader in our clubhouse and a valued member of the Red Wings family,' the organization said on Monday.



'His impact on the game and the players he mentored will never be forgotten.'

Sports.title: Courtney Lawes, 37, quits France to return to England - with move to future club set to be confirmed this week
Sports.content:
Courtney Lawes will return to English rugby for next season - raising the enticing possibility of a return to the England squad ahead of the World Cup.

The 37-year-old forward and former national captain won 105 caps for his country and five with the British & Irish Lions before retiring from Test duty after the 2023 World Cup.

Lawes has played the past two seasons with French second division side Brive, but on Monday his current employers confirmed he will move back to his homeland - with Sale Sharks appearing to be the most likely destination.

Lawes played his entire club career with Northampton before moving to Brive. Manchester-based Sale could confirm his signing as soon as Tuesday.

A move back to PREM Rugby raises the possibility that he could make himself available again for England for the 2027 World Cup.

'I'm having an experience in Brive that I'll never forget, both on and off the pitch,' Lawes said, in a French press release that did not confirm his next destination.

'I'm going to give it my all until the end of the season to finish this adventure in the best possible way. My family and I have been very warmly welcomed and we will always have Brive at heart.'

He is set to be joined at Sale next season by another current French-based England international in Stade Francis centre Joe Marchant. Alex Lozowski of Saracens will also be joining Alex Sanderson's side.

Courtney Lawes has won 105 caps for England and five for the British & Irish Lions

Sale travel to Irish giants Leinster on Saturday for a European Champions Cup quarter-final clash, but have had a disappointing PREM campaign.

They have won just three of 12 league games and director of rugby Sanderson has been keen to add a back-row to his squad. He held talks with England flanker Chandler Cunningham-South, but opted against a deal on financial grounds and Cunningham-South re-signed with Harlequins.

The 2026-27 season will be Lawes' 20th as a professional. He told Daily Mail Sport last month he feels he still has a lot to offer at the top level.

The tough-tackling back-row held talks with Leicester Tigers and was of interest to a host of other PREM clubs but Sale look to have won the race for his signature.

'I'm looking to do one more season,' Lawes said. 'That'll round me off to 20 years as a professional. I think I'm still performing at quite a high level, so I don't really want to stop yet.

'I've known Geoff Parling (Leicester head coach) for a long time. Ultimately, the offer wasn't quite right. I won't be playing for Leicester, but I appreciated the sentiment nonetheless. For a Northampton man like me to go and play for Leicester would have caused quite a ruckus.'

Opening up on his time in France, Lawes said: 'It's been fantastic. All my kids are now fluent French speakers and that's a great life skill for them. I don't regret moving out here whatsoever. The rugby's been very different, but enjoyable. It's a really good group of lads. Life's great. The weather's good. I can't really complain.'

Sports.title: Masters star who broke Augusta protocol takes huge risk again as he returns for 2026
Sports.content:
Masters star who broke Augusta protocol takes huge risk again as he returns for 2026

The Masters, which begins at Augusta National this week, has some strict rules in play

View 2 Images Jason Day's outfits have attracted plenty of attention (Image: Maddie Meyer, Getty Images)

Jason Day was among the first players to step onto the Augusta National driving range ahead of this year's Masters. The Australian, who has found himself in trouble over the past two years for his clothing choices, is believed to have been practising at the club since Friday.

‌



Day made a point of being one of the earliest players on the range and has been fine-tuning his game for three to four hours each day since. Even as temperatures soared to highs of around 28 degrees celsius, the 38-year-old has pushed through the sweltering heat in an effort to ensure he is in peak condition ahead of Thursday's opening round.

‌



Day has courted controversy with his fashion choices in recent years, with his Malbon sponsorship testing the limits of what is deemed acceptable at Augusta National. In 2024, he was handed a warning over his 'inappropriate' sweater and told to change.

‌



Last year, the world No.41 submitted his planned outfits for the week prior to the tournament and Masters officials asked him to tone down his designs. Malbon unveiled their 2026 Masters collection for Day last week, only for the club to deliver another rejection.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Who is at the Masters dinner? Guest list in full as Rory McIlroy hosts for first time READ MORE :

Masters chairman has already made Donald Trump thoughts crystal clear with president banned READ MORE :

Plain block colours appear to be favoured and the flamboyant bird design put forward by Malbon would appear to go against that preference. That said, Day was still spotted wearing the vest while practising on Monday.

‌



There can be little doubt, however, that Day has been taking his preparations as seriously as can be expected. He tied for eighth place 12 months ago, finishing on 5-under but struggling to challenge Rory McIlroy and Justin Rose as they surged clear on Sunday.

The day before, Day admitted to feeling largely powerless when McIlroy is firing on all cylinders. He even went as far as suggesting even sabotaging his rival's clubs wouldn't make a difference.

"[You] can't do anything. You want to go over there and break every club in his bag, but that's just not going to work," Day said.

‌



"He's clearly playing some good golf, so you've got to do the best job you can. I've been on the receiving end of a couple of those where he's run away with it a little bit, Congressional when I finished second there and he beat me by eight."

View 2 Images Day was handed a warning over his attire in 2024 (Image: Warren Little/Getty Images)

By arriving earlier to prepare, the 2015 PGA Championship winner may well find himself in a stronger position this time round. Day wasn't the only one turning up before Masters Monday, either.

Article continues below

Justin Thomas and Bryson DeChambeau were both spotted on the range on Sunday. Defending champion McIlroy has also been making his presence felt at the club, taking in the Augusta National Women's Amateur and Drive, Chip and Putt competitions and even taking his dad out for a round on Sunday afternoon.

As for Monday, Ryan Fox was amongst the first to hit the driving range. It marks the New Zealander's comeback after abruptly pulling out of the Players and undergoing emergency surgery for kidney stones - an ordeal the 39 year old described as "absolutely brutal."

Sports.title: Golf legend makes astonishing claim about Rory McIlroy's wife Erica Stroll and picks replacement
Sports.content:
Golf legend makes astonishing claim about Rory McIlroy's wife Erica Stroll and picks replacement

A golf legend has made a jaw-dropping claim about Rory McIlroy's wife Erica Stoll

View 2 Images Erica Stoll and Rory McIlroy nearly divorced in 2024 (Image: (David Cannon/Getty Images))

Paul McGinley has bizarrely claimed another PGA Tour golfer’s wife would be a better match for Rory McIlroy than his actual wife, Erica Stoll. McIlroy’s struggling relationship with Stoll came to light in May 2024 as the Northern Irish golfer filed for a divorce in Palm Beach County, Florida.

‌



He said at the time that his marriage was "irretrievably broken" after seven years together. Stoll shunned the spotlight and refused to do interviews or visit McIlroy on tour. But the couple made a dramatic U-turn and announced one month after the news initially broke that they had decided to stay together.

‌



Now, as he looks to defend his Masters title at Augusta National, the 36-year-old’s struggles with his wife have been laid bare in a revealing new book about the five-time major champion’s life.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alan Shipnuck's 'Rory: The Heartache and Triumph of Golf's Most Human Superstar' provides an extensive look at their relationship. In the book, McIlroy’s 2014 Team Europe Ryder Cup captain McGinley stunningly claimed McIlroy would have been better off with golf rival Padraig Harrington's wife.

McGinley began by saying: "It can't be easy being Rory's wife. I'm sure it's not easy for her because she's quiet by nature."

‌



He added: "Caroline Harrington would have been perfect as Rory's wife. She (Caroline) loves Padraig being a professional golfer more than Padraig loves being a professional golfer.

"But Erica is quiet and she kind of keeps her thoughts to herself. She's had to find where she fits in and where she doesn't." McGinley went on to say that while McIlroy is a "superstar" and has a "big personality", Stoll was not like that at all.

McIlroy married Stoll in 2017 in a star-studded ceremony at Ashford Castle in County Mayo, Ireland, where guests included Stevie Wonder. Stoll had been working for the PGA of America when she met McIlroy in 2012 at the Ryder Cup.

‌



View 2 Images Paul McGinley made a strange claim about McIlroy (Image: Getty Images)

According to his close friend Shane Lowry, 2023 was a "tough spot" for McIlroy. Golf had been a refuge for him until the divorce filing.

Announcing his decision to stay with Stoll, who is the mother of his daughter, Poppy, McIlroy said in 2024: "Erica and I have realised that our best future was as a family together." He described the ordeal as a "wake-up call".

Article continues below

Stoll has since been seen cheering on McIlroy on the greens and was targeted with abuse by the crowd at last year’s Ryder Cup. She and Poppy will likely join him for the traditional par-three contest this week as he looks to secure a second green jacket.

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy to honour Tiger Woods at Masters Dinner after icon's DUI arrest
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy to honour Tiger Woods at Masters Dinner after icon's DUI arrest

The Masters takes place this weekend and as reigning champion, Rory McIlory will host the annual dinner at Augusta National and honour previous winners including Tiger Woods

View 2 Images Tiger Woods won't be present at the Masters Champions Dinner (Image: Megan Briggs/TGL/TGL via Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy has revealed that he plans to honour the absent Tiger Woods when he hosts the Masters Champions Dinner on Tuesday. Woods, 50, was arrested last month following a rollover car crash in Florida.

Police found Woods with two opioid pain killers in his pocket and the golf icon, who pleaded not guilty to driving under the influence (DUI), has since been granted permission to seek treatment outside of the United States. It means that Woods won't be present at Augusta National when reigning Masters champion McIlroy hosts the illustrious dinner for previous winners.

Speaking at Monday's Drive, Chip and Putt event, the Northern Irishman confirmed that he'll 'acknowledge' both Woods and Phil Mickelson, who'll also be missing at the dinner because of a family health matter. "Unfortunately, there will be a couple of guys that won't be in that room, which is a shame," McIlroy explained.

"But I want to make sure that they're acknowledged as well. They've been two of the greatest champions that the Masters has ever seen.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Justin Rose answers all-important question about Masters dream after Rory McIlroy heartbreak READ MORE :

"But it's going to be a really cool night. I can't wait. I hope everyone enjoys the dinner and enjoys everything that I've selected."

Article continues below

In body camera footage during his arrest, Woods told Martin County police officers that he was 'hoping' to play in the Masters. "It depends on y'all," the five-time winner added.

Having struggled with multiple injury setbacks, Woods has played competitive golf just once in the past 21 months, and that was days before he was arrested. The 50-year-old released a statement after being released on bail.

"I know and understand the seriousness of the situation I find myself in today," Woods said. "I am stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health.

View 2 Images Tiger Woods was arrested on March 27 (Image: Martin County Sheriff's Office)

"This is necessary in order for me to prioritise my well-being and work toward lasting recovery. I'm committed to taking the time needed to return in a healthier, stronger and more focused place, both personally and professionally. I appreciate your understanding and support, and ask for privacy for my family, loved ones and myself at this time."

Brian Rolapp, CEO of the PGA Tour, also issued a statement. "Tiger Woods is one of the most influential figures the sports world has ever known," Rolapp said.

Article continues below

"Over the last year, I have come to deeply appreciate Tiger not only for his impact on the game, but for his friendship and the perspective he has shared with me as I joined the golf industry. My thoughts are with him and his family as he takes this step, for which he has my full respect and support."

The 2026 Masters begins on Thursday. Play will start after 2pm UK time.

Sports.title: Masters winner explains sudden decision to quit LIV Golf after controversial exit
Sports.content:
Masters winner explains sudden decision to quit LIV Golf after controversial exit

Augusta National will welcome one familiar face back this week as a former Masters champion opens a new chapter in his career

View 2 Images Patrick Reed has opened up about his decision to abandon LIV Golf and make a return to the PGA Tour ahead of the Masters (Image: Andrew Redington/Getty Images)

Green Jackets are a collector's item at Augusta National, but 2018 Masters champion Patrick Reed returns this week as one proud owner. And he'll do so with a few more friendly faces on his side after announcing his exit from LIV Golf.

Reed, 35, confirmed in January that he'd be parting ways with the Saudi-backed series ahead of a future return to the PGA Tour. He's not eligible to play in PGA competitions until after August, but that won't get in the way of him seeking a second Masters title this week.

The Texan was part of the initial batch of defectors to leave the PGA and jump ship to LIV in 2022. Having now reversed that decision, however, he explained his thought process and reasons for reverting back.

Speaking to Sports Illustrated ahead of the 2026 Masters, he said: "We had an offer, but at the end of the day, it was kind of one of those things that when I sat down and talked with my wife [Justine] and my team, I just felt like the best decision for us was to come back and join the PGA Tour, so I could be closer to home and with the family.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"There’s nothing that I felt like was going on between LIV and us or anything like that. As I said, we had a contract, had a deal, but at the end of the day, I felt like the best thing for us was to come to the PGA Tour again."

Who is at the Masters dinner? Guest list in full as Rory McIlroy hosts for first time READ MORE :

Patrick Reed and LIV Golf star have very different views on Tiger Woods' Masters absence READ MORE :

While he cannot play PGA Tour events until this summer, Reed is well underway regaining his status on the DP World Tour. In fact, he already has two wins on the European circuit since getting back to business at the start of the year.

Soon after announcing his LIV departure, Reed dominated the field to win the Hero Dubai Desert Classic by four strokes in January. He followed that up with a play-off loss at the Bahrain Championship, then took the Qatar Masters title, all in the space of a fortnight.

“It definitely happened quickly, but it was one of those that, when I was over there in Dubai and playing, I really just kind of was sitting back and realizing that I wanted to get back and not only join—have an opportunity back on the PGA Tour, but get back to the traditional way of golf and playing," Reed continued.

View 2 Images Reed won the Masters in 2018, several years before turning his back on the PGA to join LIV (Image: Patrick Smith/Getty Images)

"When I stood there in Dubai, that Saturday, the entire range was full, and then guys just started disappearing, and you’re the last man on that tee box. Then you’re walking to the tee, you’re the last name announced, and you’ve lost the lead because someone is five-under through eigt.

"All those just rushes and those scenarios, kind of going back into playing golf that way, where you’re going out there, and you’re having the battles between not just yourself, but the other guys on the leaderboard. For me, I wanted that back, I wanted that adrenaline back, and those feelings, especially with the way I played those last three weeks."

Article continues below

It seemed like no coincidence that Reed's own decision to return to the PGA Tour came not long after Brooks Koepka confirmed his own comeback in December. The five-time major champion was the first household name to announce he'd be leaving LIV and was granted special dispensation to return to the PGA Tour this year.

Reed described this as "the perfect time" to abandon LIV Golf as he didn't have a contract with the organisation at the time. And while he may be excluded from PGA Tour play for the time being, he's well in the running for a second Masters title after registering five top-10 finishes at Augusta across his last eight appearances.

Sports.title: Why Rory McIlroy won't sit next to Scottie Scheffler or Jordan Spieth at Masters dinner
Sports.content:
Why Rory McIlroy won't sit next to Scottie Scheffler or Jordan Spieth at Masters dinner

Rory McIlroy is hosting the annual Masters Champions Dinner ahead of the 2026 tournament at Augusta National - and won't be sitting next to any of his rivals

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler won't be sitting next to each other at the Masters Champions Dinner tonight (Image: Getty Images)

Twelve months ago, Rory McIlroy ended his long, painful wait for a Masters title. After a nervy playoff against Justin Rose, the Northern Irishman sank to his knees after rolling in the winning putt to clinch not only his first green jacket but also a historic Career Grand Slam.

‌



This week, McIlroy returns to Augusta National as the defending champion. But before a single shot is struck, he must fulfil one of the Masters' most cherished traditions: hosting the Champions Dinner, held each year on the Tuesday before the tournament.

‌



An exclusive gathering, the dinner is reserved solely for past Masters winners. As reigning champion, McIlroy takes centre stage - presiding over the evening and personally selecting the menu for a room steeped in golfing history.

‌



One interesting aspect of the dinner, which is held on the second floor of the Augusta National clubhouse, is the absence of a seating plan. That said, McIlroy's place is the one exception.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Who is at the Masters dinner? Guest list in full as Rory McIlroy hosts for first time READ MORE :

The 36-year-old will sit at the head of the table, flanked by the dinner's long-standing MC, two-time champion Ben Crenshaw and Augusta National chairman Fred Ridley.

‌



This means McIlroy will avoid having to sit next to the likes of Scottie Scheffler, Jordan Spieth or Jon Rahm - players who will be gunning for his title over the weekend.

Despite the lack of a seating plan, many attendees fall into similar routines. "A lot of people sit in the same chairs," 2013 champion Adam Scott revealed in 2023. "I like that, to be perfectly honest. I like the fact that you kind of feel like that's your spot."

Two-time winner Scheffler also pointed to the unspoken etiquette. "There's a little protocol," he said of where players tend to sit, or, for that matter, not sit. "I'm definitely not going to go sit in the area where Tiger [Woods] and Jack [Nicklaus] sit. Like, there's kind of spots where you kind of feel you'll naturally flow into."

‌



View 2 Images The annual Champions Dinner is held on the Tuesday of Masters week (Image: @TheMasters/Twitter)

Speaking ahead of the dinner, McIlroy said he felt "incredibly grateful" to finally take part. "I want to share that with everyone in the room," he said.

"It is the most exclusive dinner club in all of sport and I think we should all feel very fortunate that we are there. We're there because of the hard work and the good play that we've been able to produce."

‌



Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson won't be in attendance this year. Woods remains sidelined following last month's car crash, while Mickelson is absent due to a family-related health matter. Even so, around 30 Masters champions are expected to attend, including six-time winner Jack Nicklaus and 90-year-old three-time champion Gary Player.

"Unfortunately, there'll be a couple of guys that won't be in that room, which is a shame," Mcllroy said. "I want to make sure that they're acknowledged as well - they've been two of the greatest champions that the Masters has ever seen."

As for the menu, McIlroy has opted for an indulgent spread. Starters include peach and ricotta flatbread, rock shrimp tempura, bacon-wrapped dates and grilled elk sliders. A yellowfin tuna carpaccio follows, before a choice of main course - Wagyu filet mignon or seared salmon. Dessert is a classic: sticky toffee pudding.

Sports.title: Masters security intervene as greedy fans rush to buy item that resells for £660
Sports.content:
Masters security intervene as greedy fans rush to buy item that resells for £660

Augusta National were forced to close the gift shop line as patrons flocked to buy a limited-edition item

View 2 Images Augusta National welcomed visitors on Monday ahead of the Masters (Image: Hector Vivas/Getty Images)

The Augusta National gift shop was the first destination for many visitors after entering the legendary grounds on Masters Monday. Access to merchandise is one of the top attractions of the trip and one item has captured interest more than any other: limited-edition garden gnomes.

‌



Augusta National first unveiled a gnome in 2016, with a limited run of 13.5-inch figurines issued every year since 2018. The gnomes are priced at £37.39 ($49.50) each but their limited availability - with only roughly 1,000 on offer each day during tournament week - has transformed them into a highly sought-after collectable.

‌



The 2026 edition depicts a bearded patron holding a green-and-white Masters umbrella. The in-demand item has already appeared on the resale market, with listings sitting around £657 ($870).

‌



The original 2016 edition, wearing a green and white jumper with a golf bag draped over the shoulder, can fetch prices in the vicinity of £7,553 ($10,000). A complete collection from 2016-25 is currently listed on eBay for £30,215 ($40,000).

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Consequently, plenty of visitors were eager to secure their piece of the action after the gates opened early Monday morning. A queue five-wide and hundreds of yards long formed almost immediately.

‌



Masters chairman has already made Donald Trump thoughts crystal clear with president banned READ MORE :

One security officer called out to the enormous queue of spectators, urging attendees that they "don't need a gnome" and should instead soak up the atmosphere and beauty of the course. Augusta National staff responded by closing off the line.

The employees held up signs informing spectators that no others could enter. The line later reopened but those at the back faced an agonising wait.

The lucky few spotted carrying up to four gnomes each after gaining entry to the gift shop when it opened looked immensely pleased with their purchases. The desperation to secure a gnome has heightened this year amid rumours that Augusta National will stop selling the ceramic ornaments after this year's tournament, which begins properly on Thursday.

‌



View 2 Images Collectable gnomes have been flying off the shelves at Augusta National (Image: Leckie Wong/Augusta National/Getty Images)

The rationale behind the decision to phase out the gnomes hasn't been publicly revealed. However, the secondary-market profiteering and the countless spectators compromising their Augusta National experience for shopping have likely influenced club chairman Fred Ridley and his colleagues.

The tournament bans spectators from bringing phones onto the grounds, with media professionals only allowed to use them inside the press centre. The stringent policy encourages living in the moment and prevents people from chasing online attention by behaving inappropriately.

Article continues below

Sports.title: Masters chairman has already made Donald Trump thoughts crystal clear with president banned
Sports.content:
Masters chairman has already made Donald Trump thoughts crystal clear with president banned

Masters chairman Fred Ridley is due to make his traditional pre-tournament speech and some will be wondering if US President Donald Trump gets a mention

View 2 Images All eyes will be on Masters chairman Fred Ridley as he prepares to speak at his pre-tournament press conference (Image: AP)

Fred Ridley, chairman of the Masters, declined to mention Donald Trump in his speech ahead of the 2025 edition of the tournament and appears unlikely to give the United States president a shout-out this time either. Trump has reportedly pursued membership of Augusta National, the storied Georgia golf club where the tournament is held, though he was recently given a brutal verdict on why that is unlikely to arrive any time soon.

‌



Coaching legend Butch Harmon indicated the president will remained banned from becoming a member "because he is Trump", arguing he does not fit the profile of the type of person who is approved to be a member at Augusta National. It is one of the world's most exclusive clubs, with membership restricted to roughly 300 people at any given time.

‌



“A colder than usual January has been conducive to a near-perfect early spring bloom of azaleas,” Ridley said at the start of his 2025 press conference. The chairman also addressed the invitation handed to former champion Angel Cabrera after the Argentine served 30 months in prison but there was no mention of the commander-in-chief.

‌



Ridley's speech ahead of the 2026 event is due to take place on Wednesday. Once again, Trump's name is not expected to come up, giving an indication of where the chairman's head is at.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

When asked about Trump being overlooked for membership, Harmon - who coached the likes of Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson - made his feelings clear. "I think you can answer that yourself. Because he's Trump," the 82-year-old said.

‌



"I think he is who he is. He's full of himself. He's the type of person that I don't think fits the profile of an Augusta member. I've known him most of my whole life, because his father was a member of Winged Foot.

"I've known Donald pretty much my whole life. What you see is what you get with him. And I don't think his personality fits the membership at Augusta.

"I don't think that [being president] has anything to do with it, because there's been a lot of other presidents who played golf, and they're not members. [Bill] Clinton, [Barack] Obama... they played golf. I think it's just his personality doesn't mix with that particular club. That’s as politically correct as I can be."

‌



View 2 Images Keen golfer Trump presented Tiger Woods with the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2019 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The 2026 Masters is due to begin on Thursday. Rory McIlroy is the defending champion at Augusta, having beaten Justin Rose in a play-off last year to complete a career grand slam.

“It only boosts my belief that I can go ahead and do it,” Rose said when addressing his latest near-miss. “I've pretty much done what it takes to win. I just haven't kind of walked over the line. I feel like I've executed well enough to have done the job.

Article continues below

“From that point of view, I don't feel like I have to find something in myself or do something different. I truly believe that. No, I don't feel like [the Masters] owes me anything. I come here with a good attitude.”
